name: Avascular Necrosis of Genetic Origin

criteria.description: Progressive joint pain and limited range of motion localized to weight-bearing joints
MRI or radiographic evidence of bone ischemia and necrosis without traumatic cause
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with bone vascular supply or metabolism
Absence of secondary causes such as corticosteroid use, alcohol abuse, or trauma
Positive family history of avascular necrosis or related osteonecrosis disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation, imaging findings, genetic testing confirming pathogenic variant, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical to differentiate from idiopathic or secondary avascular necrosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic site of bone death in genetic cases
searchTerms: bone death in hip bone area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive joint stiffness in affected joints
Radiographic evidence of subchondral bone collapse
searchTerms: x-ray showing bone collapse under cartilage

common.symptomName: Intermittent joint pain exacerbated by weight-bearing
searchTerms: joint pain that comes and goes with activity
intermittent joint discomfort on weight bearing
pain worsened by standing or walking

common.symptomName: Reduced range of motion in hip or knee joints
searchTerms: limited movement in hip or knee
stiffness in hip or knee joints

common.symptomName: Limping gait due to joint discomfort
searchTerms: uneven walking caused by joint discomfort
loss of muscle bulk by joint

occasional.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever
broken bones in dead bone areas
bone tissue death in small bones
avascular necrosis in less used bones
wear and tear arthritis in joints

laboratory: Exclusion of autoimmune or infectious causes
imaging: MRI showing bone marrow edema and necrosis
X-ray demonstrating subchondral radiolucency and bone collapse
CT scan for detailed bone architecture assessment
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COL2A1, PON1, or other genes affecting bone vascularization
Family genetic screening identifying autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance patterns
other: Histopathology confirming dead bone tissue with empty lacunae
Absence of trauma or corticosteroid exposure history

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with corticosteroid use or alcohol abuse
History of joint trauma or fracture
Localized necrosis at site of injury
Lesions primarily in subchondral bone with overlying cartilage involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of joint collapse within months
Severe joint pain unresponsive to conservative treatment
